text: In June 2016 we spoke, in retrospect, of a court and a floor. Thirty-two of us said "the supreme court," peaking on June 23. Twenty-nine of us said "the house floor," and twenty-eight said "on the house floor," both peaking June 22. On June 23, twenty-eight of us said "comprehensive immigration reform," and twenty-eight said "deferred action for." Twenty-seven of us said "deferred action for childhood arrivals." Twenty-six said "parents of americans." Twenty-five said "deferred action for parents of americans." We repeated these words, and our counts fell within seven of one another, on two days. We do not here supply the ruling or its reasons. We report only that we said them, on which days, and how many of us said each.

top_phrases.phrase: deferred action for parents of americans
